newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo gold ends down sharply as yen rallies.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo gold ends down sharply as yen rallies.

text.p: TOCOM yen-based gold futures fell sharply on Thursday, battered by the yen's rally to two-week highs against the dollar.
But cash prices firmed slightly as the volatile currency market sparked opposite reactions in the bullion and Tokyo futures markets, traders said.

Bargain hunting on TOCOM this morning, after currency inspired selling from trade houses pushed prices lower, allowed yen-based futures to steady and in turn gave a light lift to bullion prices, traders said. But professional selling from overseas capped the gains and spot prices drifted back down.
TOCOM benchmark October 1997 gold ended 29 lower at 1,350 yen per gram, after hitting a one-month low of 1,347 intraday.
Bullion ended at $377.90/20 an ounce, up marginally from New York's closing quote of $377.70/20.
Today's activity focused on the tumble in the dollar, which hit a two-week low of 111.95 yen. "The sheer velocity of it took the market by surprise," said one trader.

Traders nevertheless remained bearish on gold, with producer selling from Australia and elsewhere expected to help cap any attempted rallies, while speculative funds appeared content to hold onto their large short positions.
Also undermining gold was strength in the stock and bond markets, which looked favorably on Tuesday's re-election of President Bill Clinton and a Republican-dominated Congress.
Traders pegged stiff nearby resistance for spot gold at $379 to $380, while one predicted it would soon break below support at $377 to fresh 19-month lows.

Other yen-based precious metal futures also slid on today's yen rally. TOCOM October platinum ended 24 lower at 1,366 yen per gram, October palladium was off six at 422 yen per gram and October silver went out 5.7 lower at 175.0 yen per 10 grams.
